title: Relative finite-presentation approximation of a qcqs morphism
statement: Let $f:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where both $Z$ and $S$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, a system of $S$-schemes $Z_i\to S$ of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and affine $S$-morphisms $Z_j\to Z_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism], satisfying the identity and composition laws, together with compatible $S$-morphisms $p_i:Z\to Z_i$ exhibiting $Z$ as their inverse limit in schemes. In particular $f$ is the composite of each $p_i$ with $Z_i\to S$. Each $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Inverse limit means that every compatible family of maps from a scheme to the $Z_i$ factors uniquely through $Z$.

source.place: Tag 09MV, label lemma-relative-approximation; qcqs-base special case, including qcqs stages of finite presentation over a qcqs base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-qcqs-arrow-absolute-approximation] to $f:Z\to S$. Write the resulting arrows as $h_i:A_i\to B_i$, the projections as $u_i:Z\to A_i$ and $v_i:S\to B_i$, and the transitions as $a_{ji},b_{ji}$. Thus $h_i u_i=v_i f$, $Z=\varprojlim A_i$, $S=\varprojlim B_i$, and both systems have affine transitions and qcqs stages of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. The index set is small, nonempty and directed.

The node [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives that $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian. Apply [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] to the finite-type structural map $A_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, obtaining local finite presentation. Both structural maps are locally of finite type; applying [lem-a1-map-over-base-finite-presentation] over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ therefore makes $h_i:A_i\to B_i$ locally of finite presentation. Its source and target are qcqs, so clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $h_i$. Hence $h_i$ is of finite presentation, meaning precisely locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

Put $Z_i=A_i\times_{B_i}S$ using $v_i$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with structure map $r_i:Z_i\to S$ the second projection. It is the base change of $h_i$, so clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] makes it of finite presentation. Clause (2), with the qcqs base $S$, makes $Z_i$ qcqs. Define the transition $t_{ji}:Z_j\to Z_i$ by the pair $(a_{ji}\operatorname{pr}_{A_j},\operatorname{pr}_S)$; it is defined because $h_i a_{ji}=b_{ji}h_j$ and $v_i=b_{ji}v_j$. The identity and composition laws hold since their composites with both projections agree. Apply the affine-transition conclusion of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products] to the three systems $(A_i),(B_i)$ and the constant system $(S)$ with maps $v_i:S\to B_i$. All three sets of transitions are affine, the last being identities. Consequently all $t_{ji}$ are affine. Each $t_{ji}$ is over $S$ by its second component.

The constant system $(S)$ has limit $S$: a compatible family of maps into it is constant, because any two indices have an upper bound. The limit comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-limit-fibre-products] therefore identifies the limit of $(Z_i)$ with $Z\times_S S$, where the maps to $S$ are $f$ and the identity. Its first projection is an isomorphism with inverse $(\mathrm{id}_Z,f)$: both composites are identities by the two projection equations [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus the cone from $Z$ has projections $p_i=(u_i,f)$, and it is limiting in schemes. Explicitly, a compatible family $T\to Z_i$ supplies compatible maps $T\to A_i$ and one common map $T\to S$; the cited limit comparison gives their unique map to $Z\times_S S$, and the displayed isomorphism gives a unique map $T\to Z$. Its composites are the given family. Finally $r_i p_i=f$ by the second projection, which proves every compatibility and the claimed factorization of $f$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_qcqs_relative_finitePresentation_approximation {Z S : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace Z] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Z] [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] (f : Z ⟶ S) : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)) (_ : Nonempty I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (q : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj S) (π : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Z ⟶ D), (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (q.app i) ∧ QuasiCompact (q.app i) ∧ QuasiSeparated (q.app i)) ∧ (∀ (i j : Iᵒᵖ) (h : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map h)) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, π.app i ≫ q.app i = f) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i) ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk Z π))
